text: 🇲🇽🌎 "They say we are being left all alone in Latin America. Well, not so much, right? The people protect us, just as we protect the people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 Sheinbaum closed Tuesday's mañanera, with the full security cabinet on stage, by putting up a chart published the day before. "We'll just leave it there."

🇲🇽✊ "We have not been sitting with our arms crossed. We have spent two years working intensely." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 Ahead of today's protest by IMSS workers, Sheinbaum laid out two years of health work: 34 new hospitals with 1,840 beds, 650 operating rooms rehabilitated (capacity for 370,000 more surgeries a year), 22,456 doctors and 21,074 nurses hired. Still pending: raising residents' stipends, some as low as 7,000 pesos a month, and proper contracts for staff hired during COVID. "It is not fair that in COVID they were asked for an extraordinary effort and that today they do not have the best working conditions." The protest will be attended, she said, and it must be peaceful.

🇲🇽⚖️ "They will not be centers operated by private companies, as in the previous period." "There are people who believe detainees have no rights, and the human rights of all people must always be respected." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 With 70,000 people arrested since this government took office, some state prisons are overcrowded. The federal government will help build six new prisons in Chiapas, State of Mexico, Nayarit, Sinaloa, Sonora and Veracruz, for 18,480 people, run by federal or state security agencies, with space to work, exercise and study. Sheinbaum stressed that far more schools are being built: 401 new high schools in 2025–2026 and about 100,000 new university places. "Education is the best instrument against violence."

🇲🇽🔍 "September 2026 is the lowest September since 2015." — Marcela Figueroa, Executive Secretary of the National Public Security System, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 Two years into Sheinbaum's term, the daily average of intentional homicides fell 52%, from 86.9 in September 2024 to 42.2 in September 2026: 45 fewer homicides every day. Colima is down 85%, Guanajuato 72% from its February 2025 peak, Guerrero 60% and Baja California 43%. All 32 states are down so far this year compared with 2025. High-impact crimes fell 36% and violent car theft 55%. Since October 2024, 70,500 people have been arrested and 36,300 firearms and 569 tons of drugs seized.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Food Basket Up 5.5% in Cities, Wage Still Covers It Twice</u>

INEGI: the urban food basket rose 5.5% year over year in September, above general inflation of 3.5%, pushed by onion, tomato and meals eaten outside the home. The full urban poverty line (food plus non-food) now stands at 4,951.66 pesos per person per month, up 4.4%.

The 2026 minimum wage of 9,582 pesos a month covers that line almost twice over. In 2018 it didn't even cover one (El Economista).

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Six New Federal-Funded Prisons, Zero Private Operators</u>

García Harfuch announced six new state prisons in Sinaloa, Sonora, Chiapas, Nayarit, Veracruz and Estado de México, with 18,480 spaces. Construction starts in Sinaloa, and all six are due by 2028.

Sheinbaum says they will be built with federal money and will not be run by private companies. That breaks with the Calderón–Peña Nieto model of private "CPS" prisons and their decades-long contracts. The design includes schooling, job training and post-release employment.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena to Lemus: Free the Water Protesters</u>

Morena demanded the release of the people detained after Jalisco police broke up Sunday's march for clean water at Casa Jalisco. Its message to Movimiento Ciudadano's governor was that repression will never be the way.

The count so far: 39 arrested, 31 civilians needing medical care, and only 18 released. The protest was over Guadalajara's water crisis and fears of privatization.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>China to Mexico: Your Ties With Washington Shouldn't Dictate Who You Trade With</u>

Beijing's special envoy for Latin America, Qiu Xiaoqi (ambassador to Mexico 2013–2019), said China values Mexico–US relations, but they must not affect Mexico's trade with third countries, China included.

He said Mexico has "enough wisdom and experience to handle this properly." The message lands as Mexico's new tariffs on countries without trade agreements hit more than $30 billion in Chinese exports.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Homicides Down 52% in Two Years</u>

Mexico's daily homicide average fell from 86.9 in September 2024 to 42.2 in September 2026, according to the SESNSP. That's 45 fewer murders every single day, and the lowest September since 2015.

All 32 states are down in the first nine months of 2026 vs. 2025. San Luis Potosí leads at −78.6%, then Nayarit at −69.5% and Quintana Roo at −59.7%.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Mexico's Farm Trade Stays in Surplus Despite US Tariffs: $4.28 Billion</u>

Mexico's agri-food trade posted a $4.283 billion surplus from January to August 2026, El Economista reports, down 13.1% from $4.931 billion a year earlier. Exports rose 2.5% to $36.035 billion while imports grew 5.1% to $31.752 billion, as tougher US tariffs hit beer, avocado, berries and sugar, and a stronger peso cut exporters' earnings.
